Quick update (SRE):
- We saw the anomalies at 08:46 PDT in us-west-2 serving tier for the hosted API.
- Root cause (initial): an autoscaler loop combined with a spike in long-tail seq len requests that caused inefficient batching and KV cache thrash. This produced multi-second tail latencies on a subset of GPU backends.
- Immediate mitigations applied at 09:15 PDT: pinned model variant to v1.14 (reverted a recent kernel/quantization path), disabled continuous rebalancing for affected pools, and tightened batching window to lower tail.
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260717-1 (incident created at 09:20 PDT). We also created JIRA INF-4721 to track the engineering follow-ups.

Observed impact: p95 reduced from ~1.8s to ~420ms after mitigations; p99 reduced from ~4s to ~950ms. Continuing to monitor.

Attachments: latency_graphs_2026-07-17.png (attached) — contains service-wide percentile plots and per-backend histograms.

Next steps (72h):
- deeper postmortem to confirm kernel selection regression and autoscaler policy gap
- add prefix-based caching safeguards for customer workloads with long contexts
- reconcile rollout process to prevent quantization/path changes without canary in high-qps regions

I'll draft the postmortem and share for review.

—Neha

Subject: Postmortem draft: us-west-2 p95/p99 regression on 2026-07-17

Team — draft postmortem attached (postmortem_draft_2026-07-19.docx). Summary below for review before we publish:

Incident window: 08:46 PDT — 09:45 PDT (mitigation applied 09:15; residual tail until ~09:45).
Impact: Elevated p95/p99 for hosted API in us-west-2 causing ingestion timeouts for a small subset of high-qps customers (notably ACME Air).
Root cause: A canary for a quantization/kernel selection change promoted across pools without adequate long-context canaries. This, combined with an autoscaler rebalance triggered by a correlated burst of long-context requests, caused repeated KV cache invalidations and inefficient batching.
Contributing factors:
- rollout gating lacked a long-tail context test (missing workload-shaped canary)
- autoscaler policy allowed repeated scale churn in limited time windows
- no automatic rollback trigger for p99 spikes in the control loop

Remediations (owner / ETA):
- Add workload-shaped long-context canaries to rollout pipeline (owner: Jonas Weber, ETA: 3w).
- Implement autoscaler dampening for short-lived spikes (owner: Dylan Brooks, ETA: 2w).
- Add p99-triggered rollback to kernel selection pipeline (owner: Neha Kapoor, ETA: 1w).
- Customer outreach & credits (owner: Marissa Cole / Finance, ETA: 3 business days).

Please review and send edits by EOD Monday so we can publish the incident summary to status.redwood.ai and send ACME the final postmortem.

—Neha
